title: Improving Legal Judgement Prediction in Romanian with Long Text Encoders
authors: Mihai Masala, Traian Rebedea, Horia Velicu
text:
The Transformer architecture [1] initially proposed for machine translation has become almost ubiquitous for many Machine Learning tasks. Transformer based architectures [2,3] are used to develop state-of-the-art solution in a variety of fields, ranging from Natural Language Processing [4,5] to Computer Vision [6,7], Audio Signal Processing [8] and image/video synthesis [9,10]. Recently, Large Language Models [11] became capable of understanding and producing human-like text, leading to the advent of powerful conversational agents [12,13,14]. Besides capable of engaging in human-like conversations, due to the huge amounts of pre-training and fine-tuning data, LLMs obtain state-of-the-art results on several tasks [15].

Nevertheless, especially for highly specialized domains, there is still a need for custom models and methods. As such, legal [16,17,18,19,20], medical [21,22,23], chemical [24,25] or financial [26,27,28,29] models have been proposed for a variety of languages.

In this work we investigate how to effectively process the long documents in the legal domain for a low-resource language (Romanian). We experiment with four different datasets, provided by a one of the top banks in Romania, from two different sources. We are, to the best of our knowledge, the first to prove that SLED [30] encoding applied on long documents for the legal judgement prediction tasks significantly improves performance compared to baseline methods. This is especially important for low-resource languages, such as Romanian, where language-specific LLMs with long-context support are not yet available and existing multi-language LLMs have low performance, at least for Romanian as this study demonstrates.

The main takeaways from the experiments are that: 1) encoding long documents with SLED can provide an important increase of performance, 2) multi-lingual LLMs are currently under-performing on LJP in Romanian both on smaller and larger documents.
